judged_text: In updateEvent, the fallback lookup `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares each calendar's externalId against undefined and never matches. When no explicit externalCalendarId is passed (the common path, since old booking references and the new no-credentialId path store none), selectedCalendar is undefined and the update is issued against Google's default 'primary' calendar instead of the calendar the event actually lives in, leaving the real event stale/never updated.

When no explicit externalCalendarId is passed (the common path, since old booking references and the new no-credentialId path store none), selectedCalendar is undefined and the update is issued against Google's default 'primary' calendar instead of the calendar the event actually lives in, leaving the real event stale/never updated.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now sets `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to `externalCalendarId` which is `undefined`, so it will almost always return `undefined`. That makes `selectedCalendar` undefined and the subsequent `events.update` call will not target the intended calendar (and may fall back to the wrong calendar or fail). The same flawed pattern is also introduced in `deleteEvent`’s `calendarId` computation.
